purpose: Test whether native target distance inversions persist when entire agent/block shapes stay on canvas.
candidate_axis: Use each version’s unique candidate axis without padding or silent scene exclusions.
reference_rule: One true trajectory as anchor; all other true trajectories as alternative outputs; compare every unordered pair of alternatives, excluding the anchor itself.
metric: Per-scene reversed / both-strict ordering comparisons; mean scenes; physical and latent ties reported separately. Not ICL error rate.
strong_subset: RMS error ratio at least 2 and larger error at least 1 task unit.

bootstrap.unit: source cluster, same resampled sources for old/new differences

unchanged_subset: Unique candidates with factor 1 and exactly unchanged actions; require at least 3 unique candidates, report coverage separately.
limits: This uses true target features, not model predictions.
Changing future action sequences changes the error distribution. Old/new differences are not a pure visibility causal effect or a model-training gain.
Evidence can refute an offscreen-only explanation but cannot assign all remaining reversals to encoder defects.
Two-dimensional agent coordinates or selected poses are not complete physical state.
No new model inference, training, data synthesis or benchmark score replacement.
